title: Service of Notice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019

content.scenario: A consumer files a complaint against a company for defective goods. The District Commission serves a notice on the company by registered post acknowledgment due, but the company refuses to accept the notice.
content.outcome: The District Commission declares that the notice has been duly served on the company, as the notice was properly addressed, pre-paid, and duly sent by registered post acknowledgment due, and the company's refusal to accept the notice does not affect the validity of the service.

user_queries: How is a notice served on a company under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
What happens if a company refuses to accept a notice?
Can a notice be served by electronic means?
